KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...

A very cold rain continues across northern NH and much of 
western ME this evening. The main rain shield has filled in 
quite well to the north, while weak low pressure rides along a 
north progressing warm front. 

Along the coast and interior, onshore flow has kept much of the
area socked in with low clouds and fog for the day. This has 
stifled temperatures, along with NE winds reinforcing an active
cold air dam setup. Guidance is within a couple degrees of 
observations, but few capture the cooler reality of this 
stubborn air.

Low level SE winds are present, as observed in downslope
locations NW of the Whites, but it will take awhile for these 
to overcome a stout low level inversion. The cool low level 
temperatures have allowed higher peaks in western ME to see 
freezing rain and light snow through the event, with MWN also 
reporting light freezing rain.

The unique setup thickens, as an EML approaches from the west
this evening. Stratiform rain should become more showery into
the mid to late evening as elevated instability increases.
Continued to mention thunder for the overnight period, and can't
rule out an isolated instance of small hail should any higher
CAPE values materialize.

A cold front will then slide through the area Wednesday, with
upslope clouds and light precip continuing, but most cloud cover
thinning downwind of the mtns with breezy WNW winds. These will
be felt the most in the Whites and western ME mtns where wind
chills will continue well below freezing in the brisk NW winds.
These continued winter conditions could catch some fall hikers 
off guard as valley temperatures warm to the 50s to 60s, and 
those along the coast rebound to the low to mid 70s.

Cooler, drier, and not as breezy into Thursday as temp values 
fall behind the cold front, but manage to rise into the 50s to
around 60 outside of the mountains.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...

Low pressure will be strengthening through the Great Lakes
Thursday night as a sharp mid level trough digs through
Michigan. Regional jet dynamics will be supportive of a low 
that continues to strengthen through Saturday morning into the 
Canadian Maritimes.

This should bring another round of beneficial rain to the area,
in addition to blustery conditions behind (see KM3). Rain should
be underway Friday morning for NH, increasing east into western
ME by noon. The storm is progressive, so rain won't linger much
more than 8 to 12 hours in one location. Winds quickly shift NW
Friday evening, and this will begin a period of CAA and upslope
rain/snow showers for the mountains lasting through Saturday.

NBM QPF continues to trend greater for this event, but values
remain below that of today's system...around three quarters of
an inch. Wintry precip will again be possible with this event,
with the first round bound to higher elevations Friday morning.
The second round, with more confidence, will be associated with
the cooler NW winds arriving Friday night into Saturday. These
snow showers could fall more widespread across northern NH and 
western ME, mainly in the mountains but perhaps some snow 
showers spill into the foothills given the broad 35 to 40 kt low
level wind field.

KEY MESSAGE 3 DESCRIPTION...

Forecast confidence is above average for a blustery weekend 
with well below normal temperatures for mid-October. A strong 
surface cold front will push of the coast early Saturday 
morning, with strong NW flow in its wake as a mid level trough 
axis swings overhead. Anomalous NW flow from 850mb to the 
surface will support a gusty day with the potential for power 
outage impacts, especially in the eastern lee-sides of the 
mountains in downslope favored areas. Will have to watch this 
trend through the week, but gusts 40+ mph are possible. In 
addition to the winds, it will be cold with wind chill 
temperatures making it feel more like winter than fall. Higher 
elevations will experience full on winter conditions and will be
dangerous above the tree line, fall hiking is not recommended. 
Cold weather will continue through the weekend with sub-freezing
temperatures possible Saturday and Sunday night.
